quote.text: … we find beauty not in the thing itself, but in the patterns of shadows, the light and darkness, that one thing against another creates…
quote.author: Jun’ichirō Tanizaki, In Praise of Shadows (1933)

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The Geneva Watch Auction
stories.headline: An F.P. Journe of 2002 beat a 1945 steel Patek by 2.4 million francs
stories.dek: Phillips sold the Chronomètre à Résonance “Régence” for CHF 8,680,500 on Saturday. The steel reference 1436 made CHF 6,267,000, 57 per cent above its top estimate.

stories.headline: UNESCO’s evaluation body has recommended inscribing Japanese shodō
stories.dek: Japan’s culture agency announced the recommendation on 5 November; the committee decides in Xiamen between 1 and 3 December. China’s calligraphy was inscribed in 2009.

stories.headline: Singapore Airlines showed its 2027 cabins and moved the date again
stories.dek: More than S$2bn across 72 aircraft, unveiled on 6 November. First and Business now enter service in the second half of 2027, six years after the original date.

stories.kicker: The World · The Strait of Hormuz
stories.headline: CENTCOM takes its Iran blockade ashore as a seafarer dies in the Gulf
stories.dek: Task Force Iron Gate went after Iranian land and Caspian routes on 7 November. IMF PortWatch logged one transit of the strait on 1 November, against a pre-war 85 a day.

stories.headline: M1 and Doctor Anywhere disclose breaches hours apart, neither giving a number
stories.dek: M1 found its breach on 30 October and lists identity-card numbers among the data taken; Doctor Anywhere became aware on 29 October. Both statements landed on 6 November.

stories.headline: Hawkins publishes no operating pressure for its cookers; Fissler publishes three
stories.dek: America’s Test Kitchen measured eight stovetop cookers in November 2025 and only Fissler’s Vitaquick Premium reached 250 degrees. Kuhn Rikon still sells a valve for a 1997 pot.

stories.headline: Ohio and Maine voters limited data centres in 40 of 41 local measures
stories.dek: Ballotpedia counted 27 approved restrictions, five of them outright bans, on 3 November. Two days later the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 12.25 per cent.

stories.headline: Laowa put the first f/2 tilt-shift lens on sale, covering Fujifilm medium format
stories.dek: The 24mm Zero-D shipped on 5 November at US$1,249 in six mounts, covering medium format. No independent laboratory has measured it, and there is no Singapore price.

stories.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero took $14.5m in North America on its first day
stories.dek: GKIDS opened it on 3,254 screens on 6 November, $6.7m of that in previews. In Japan it has passed a million admissions since its Culture Day release.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · Social Media By School Stage
stories.headline: A meta-analysis in Clinical Child Psychology finds the middle years least affected
stories.dek: Han, Meng and Yang, published on 6 November, put the primary-school correlation at 0.367 and the middle-school one at 0.201. The difference is statistically significant.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Breakeven Rally
stories.headline: The ten-year Treasury yield fell five basis points while its real rate rose one
stories.dek: Brent’s sixteen per cent collapse did the work, not the Federal Reserve. Futures price a 73 per cent chance of a rise on 9 December and no chance at all of a cut.

stories.headline: A Faroese trial missed its own main target and still raised peak oxygen uptake
stories.dek: Published this month in Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports, the fourteen-week study of 111 adults aged 40 to 70 found no lean-mass gain at all.

stories.kicker: The Diary · The Studio Ghibli Premiere
stories.headline: Gardens by the Bay will premiere The Story of Studio Ghibli in December
stories.dek: It runs from 18 December to 4 July on the West Lawn, and no admission price has been published. ART SG’s early-bird tickets lapse on 24 November.

stories.headline: Karnataka charges platforms fifty paise a delivery under its Gig Workers Act
stories.dek: Five Indian states have legislated a per-transaction levy on platform work. Karnataka collected about ₹4 crore in a quarter against its own projection of ₹250–300 crore a year.
